subject.title: fix(doctor): exit non-zero on final invalid config (#77804)

question: Should residual invalid config make the human-oriented plain `openclaw doctor` command exit 1, or should non-zero validation gating remain exclusive to `doctor --lint`?
rationale: Both behaviors are technically implementable, but changing plain doctor's established exit semantics can break existing inspection, repair, update, and wrapper workflows; repository policy requires explicit intent for that compatibility choice.

options.title: Keep failure gating in lint
options.body: Preserve plain doctor's existing exit behavior, use `doctor --lint` for automation, and narrow any remaining patch to clearer error-state completion output.

options.title: Make plain doctor fail
options.body: Approve exit 1 for residual invalid config, then require a caller audit, upgrade-facing documentation, and built-CLI proof for valid, invalid, repair, and update-finalization paths.

recommendation.title: Keep failure gating in lint
recommendation.body: Preserve plain doctor's existing exit behavior, use `doctor --lint` for automation, and narrow any remaining patch to clearer error-state completion output.
